info.bio: Spinal Tap es un grupo semificticio de heavy metal creado en 1984 a partir de la película documental This Is Spinal Tap, considerada por muchos como una película de culto. El grupo existe tanto en la ficción, en que sus miembros son los personajes interpretados por los actores de la película, como en la realidad, en que los actores han grabado discos como la banda homónima. También hacen una breve aparición en un capítulo de Los Simpsons.

scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Fuera de MTV el vídeo es un medio especializado que los fans compran: recopilaciones (Fuel for Life de Judas Priest), conciertos (Live After Death de Iron Maiden), documentales al modo de The Song Remains the Same de Led Zeppelin, cintas-revista y promociones de sellos independientes de thrash como Combat y Metal Blade. Metallica deconstruye el formato con Cliff ’em All, homenaje a Cliff Burton hecho con grabaciones caseras y piratas. El cine, que necesita un público de masas, apenas trata el metal, salvo como banda sonora de películas de terror. Las dos películas sobre él de los ochenta, This Is Spinal Tap (1984), la parodia de Rob Reiner, y The Decline of Western Civilization Part II: The Metal Years (1988) de Penelope Spheeris, dan placer al público metal pero aún más a sus detractores: una es una crítica cultural de la falta de sofisticación; la otra, una crítica moral de la depravación, estrenada tras los ataques del PMRC. Spinal Tap acabó saliendo de gira de verdad.

podcast.title: Adoption of the "Rock Dot" Umlaut
podcast.body: Spinal Tap, a fictional band, is included in the list of groups that used the umlaut (or "rock dot") in their name, highlighting the widespread adoption of this stylistic choice in rock and metal music. "There's Motley Crew, Queen's Reich, Spinal Tap, Green Jelly, Motorhead, Maximal Park, Moxie Frouze, and tons of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: The band is the subject of the 1996 film "Hardcore Logo," which is often referred to as a Canadian version of "Spinal Tap" but is considered to be more substantial. "Call it a Canadian version of spinal tap if you want but that's selling it short."

xref.title: Adoption of the "Rock Dot" Umlaut
xref.body: Mötley Crüe is among the many bands that adopted the umlaut (or "rock dot") in their name, following the trend initiated by Blue Oyster Cult. This was done primarily for its aesthetic appeal, making the name look foreign, gothic, exotic, or menacing. "There's Motley Crew, Queen's Reich, Spinal Tap, Green Jelly, Motorhead, Maximal Park, Moxie Frouze, and tons of others."

xref.title: Mariah O'Brien's Cover Shoot
xref.body: Mariah O'Brien, known for appearing on Spinal Tap's "Bitch School" single, posed for the *Dirt* album cover on June 14, 1992. She lay in the body-shaped hole in the studio's "desert" set for eight hours while photographer Rocky Schenk took hundreds of shots and adjusted lighting. O'Brien later recalled having to hold her urge to urinate during the lengthy session. It was clarified that O'Brien, not singer Layne Staley's then-girlfriend Demri Parrott, is the woman on the cover. Today, Mariah O'Brien works as an interior designer in Los Angeles. "Mariah had to lie in that hole for eight hours as Schenk took hundreds of shots, adjusting the lighting countless times."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vampire Conspiracy Theory
xref.body: The theory that Dave Gahan is a vampire arose in the early 90s due to his wasted appearance from heroin and cocaine addiction, his belief in his own "rock god hype," and his commissioning of a coffin-shaped bed for pre-show naps on tour. Further fueling the rumor was an alleged incident where he bit a journalist on the neck backstage, along with bizarre behaviors like painting his entire house black. Pictures of a "vampiric looking" Gahan with fangs circulated as the public internet was emerging. Gahan himself stated in a 2001 interview that he "definitely could have been a vampire in my own head," confirming he slept in a huge double coffin-shaped bed in Los Angeles, describing his life at the time as "Spinal Tap." "I definitely could have been a vampire in my own head. Even the bed I slept in in Los Angeles was in the shape of a coffin, a huge double bed shaped like a coffin. My whole life was spinal tap at that time."
